When your population gets large enough, small changes can in fact have major repercussions due to the fact that different areas are often interdependent. This is an intended facet of the game so that you are less likely to hit a point where you're too big to fail.

I've found that it is best to delay playing with taxes, playing with policy, and making specialized zones until you have a well developed city that has slowed in growth and/or is starting to shrink a bit. This is the point where you need to set zones and play with policy--one at a time to measure the effect. Play with your zoning and make sure to place buffer zones between industrial and your commercial and residential areas--office zones are good for this. Try to reduce noise as well, this will help things level up and bring in more taxes. Make sure that you have area with both low and high density residential and commercial, this balances out the type of people that come into the city. And for gods sake, get the auto bulldoze mod.
